bibliography.title: Structural design and biomechanical analysis of anti- subsidence gradient porous artificial vertebrae combined with a topology framework
bibliography.authors: Shang P, Wu X, Li R, Ma B, Wu H, Liu Y.

study.research_problem: Traditional titanium mesh cages and non-gradient porous artificial vertebrae can have limited endplate contact, stress concentration, subsidence risk, and stiffness mismatch while greater porosity can reduce structural strength.
study.exact_gap: A topology-optimized macro-framework combined with an axially graded gyroid TPMS was proposed to balance cortical-like strength, cancellous-like porosity, interface stress, and subsidence resistance, but required FE comparison and physical testing against common AVI designs.
study.objective_or_hypothesis: Design a patient-informed AVI with a 45% topology volume fraction and a 40% central/70% end-region gyroid gradient, then test whether it lowers FE stress and increases quasi-static subsidence/compression performance versus TMC and truss+fluorite controls.
study.study_design: Mixed computational-experimental research. One healthy 26-year-old male L1-L5 CT model was used for six physiological postures and three postoperative AVI models; baseline ROM was compared with cadaver and prior FE ranges. Ti-6Al-4V specimens were SLM-printed with three replicates per type, heat-treated, and tested in grade-15 polyurethane for ASTM F2267-04 subsidence and BS ISO 13314:2011 compression. Nominal overall porosity was 55% (ends 70%, center 40%) and as-built porosity deviated by <2%.
study.sample_or_model: Patient-informed AVI geometry plus one healthy male L1-L5 anatomy; SIMP design-domain fraction 45%; gyroid block 10 x 10 x 20 mm, 2.5-mm cells, 0.27-0.54 mm walls, 710-1040 micrometre pores; SLM Ti-6Al-4V with n=3 per implant type for each mechanical test; TMC and truss+fluorite controls.
comparators: Flexion, extension, left/right bending, left/right rotation
method_spine: Set CT-informed AVI geometry and run SIMP under a 10 Nm torque with 45% design volume.
Generate a gyroid with 40% central and 70% end porosity for 55% nominal total porosity.
Build healthy and postoperative L1-L5 FE models with bone, discs, ligaments, and bonded implant interfaces.
Compare implant and adjacent-vertebra von Mises stress across six postures.
Print Ti-6Al-4V by SLM, verify porosity, and run triplicate subsidence/compression tests with load-displacement and failure modes.

verification: No formal mesh-convergence or solver-verification result is reported; dimensions and 55% porosity target were specified, and SLM porosity was checked against design (S005:C01; S014:C01).
calibration: No FE material/contact parameters were fitted to AVI curves; literature tissue properties and a 45% SIMP fraction were adopted (S005:C01; S007:C01).
validation: Healthy-model intervertebral ROM was compared with human cadaver and prior FE ranges, supporting the baseline spine model (S011:C01). Implant stress was not directly measured; triplicate bench tests are separate device evidence (S014:C01-S015:C01).
sensitivity: Six posture directions and two controls give a controlled comparison, but no systematic anatomy, porosity, contact, material, topology, or uncertainty sensitivity was reported (S012:C01-S013:C01).
application_prediction: Lower stress and higher 3-mm subsidence/compression performance are mechanical predictions or bench outcomes for this design; osteointegration, fusion, fatigue, and clinical safety remain untested (S016:C01-S017:C01).

primary_outcomes: Gradient gyroid nominal porosity was 55% overall, 70% at ends and 40% centrally, with 710-1040 micrometre pores; reported modulus/yield strength were 7.13 GPa/197.54 MPa and SLM porosity was within 2% of design (S006:C01; S014:C01).
Topology+Gyroid reduced implant peak stress by 29.5%-69.7% versus TMC across six postures and reduced adjacent-interface stress by posture-dependent amounts up to 44.3% (S012:C01-S013:C01).
Versus truss+fluorite, implant peak stress fell 10.6%-23.4% and interface stress about 5.9%-14.1% for stated upper/lower conditions (S012:C01; S016:C01).
Triplicate 3-mm subsidence loads were 2714 +/- 22 N for topology+gyroid, 2232 +/- 28 N for truss+fluorite, and 1298 +/- 13 N for TMC; topology+gyroid was 21.6% above truss+fluorite (S014:C01).

Compression stiffness/yield were 63.97 +/- 0.35 kN/mm and 54.33 +/- 0.97 kN for topology+gyroid, 11.6%/14.1% above truss+fluorite and 63.3%/124% above TMC; failure was localized and the top remained intact at 3 mm (S015:C01).
study.highest_evidence_level_reached: Mixed FE comparison with baseline ROM benchmarking and triplicate as-built quasi-static Ti-6Al-4V tests; no independent implant-stress validation, fatigue, biological, fusion, or clinical evidence.

argument_map.central_claim: A topology-optimized macro-framework plus gradient gyroid microstructure improves stress distribution and quasi-static subsidence/compression behavior versus TMC and truss+fluorite within the tested geometry.
data: SIMP framework and gradient gyroid parameters define the two-scale design (S005:C01; S006:C01).
FE posture results show lower implant and bone-interface peak stress for topology+gyroid than controls (S012:C01-S013:C01).
As-built triplicate tests show higher 3-mm subsidence load, stiffness, yield load, and localized failure (S014:C01-S015:C01).
argument_map.warrant: Larger contact area and graded porosity can reduce stress concentration while retaining load-bearing material, conditional on anatomy, interface, and loading assumptions.
backing: Baseline ROM agreement with cadaver/prior FE data provides a limited check of the spinal loading environment (S011:C01).
Measured porosity remained near the nominal 55% target, linking design intent to as-built specimens (S014:C01).
argument_map.qualifier: Applies to one patient-informed L3-L4 context, Ti-6Al-4V SLM samples, bonded FE interfaces, polyurethane subsidence blocks, and quasi-static loads.
rebuttals_or_boundaries: Quasi-static compression cannot evaluate fatigue and porosity defects may alter cyclic behavior (S016:C01).
Only one anatomy, vertebral context, and TPMS design were studied (S016:C02).
Bone ingrowth/osteointegration are rationale, not measured outcomes.
Healthy ROM validation checks the baseline spine model, not implant stress fields.

measured: SLM porosity deviation, triplicate load-displacement curves, 3-mm subsidence load, compression stiffness/yield, and observed failure stages are measured bench outcomes (S014:C01-S015:C01).
Healthy-model ROM was compared with external cadaver/FE ranges, a baseline benchmark rather than implant measurement (S011:C01).
predicted: Topology optimization, implant/adjacent-vertebra von Mises stress fields, and posture-specific reductions are FE predictions (S005:C01; S012:C01-S013:C01).
inferred: Larger contact area and elastic-modulus matching are inferred mechanisms for lower stress/subsidence (S012:C01; S016:C01).
Porous connectivity is inferred to promote osteointegration, but no bone ingrowth endpoint was obtained (S006:C01; S016:C02).
recommended: Use multiple anatomies/levels, compare TPMS designs, add fatigue/cyclic loading, quantify interface/bone ingrowth, and perform animal or long-term in-vivo validation (S016:C02).
proxy_to_outcome_bridges: FE interface stress is a mechanical proxy, not endplate remodeling, fusion, or clinical subsidence.
Polyurethane-block 3-mm settlement is a bench proxy and does not reproduce osteoporotic endplate, surgery, or long-term cycles.
Compression stiffness/yield and fracture mode do not establish fatigue durability or survival.
Nominal/as-built porosity agreement supports manufacturing fidelity, not biological integration.
overclaim_risks: The conclusion calls the implant a promising clinical treatment despite no biological, fatigue, or patient-outcome evidence (S017:C01).
Long-term postoperative and osteointegration language exceeds quasi-static/bonded-model evidence (S016:C01).
A modulus that approaches cortical bone and lower stress do not establish safety across bone quality or anatomy.
Healthy ROM validation may be misread as implant-stress validation.

section_moves.move: Frame macro and micro criteria as a coupled gap
section_moves.execution: The introduction separates topology optimization for framework strength from gradient gyroid design for stress/porosity, then motivates their combination (S002:C01-S002:C02).
section_moves.transferable_principle: For hierarchical implants, state what each scale controls and why one alone is insufficient.
section_moves.failure_mode: Two design labels without scale-specific endpoints obscure the mechanism.

section_moves.move: Separate nominal architecture, process state, and as-built verification
section_moves.execution: The porosity gradient, pore sizes, wall thickness, SLM process, heat treatment, and <2% porosity deviation are reported before testing (S006:C01; S009:C01; S014:C01).
section_moves.transferable_principle: Report nominal architecture, manufacturing route/post-processing, and measured as-built deviation as distinct states.
section_moves.failure_mode: A nominal 55% porosity can be treated as fabricated geometry if deviation is omitted.

section_moves.move: Pair posture-resolved FE fields with device load-displacement outcomes
section_moves.execution: Six-posture stress comparisons are followed by triplicate subsidence, stiffness/yield, and failure-mode results (S012:C01-S015:C01).
section_moves.transferable_principle: Align numerical and experimental outcomes by mechanical question while preserving evidence status.
section_moves.failure_mode: Bench ranking agreement does not prove FE stress magnitudes.

section_moves.move: State fatigue, biology, anatomy, and translation firewalls
section_moves.execution: The discussion notes quasi-static limits, one anatomy/TPMS, and missing osteointegration/long-term studies (S016:C01-S016:C02).
section_moves.transferable_principle: End a favorable mechanical interpretation with missing tests and the claims they constrain.
section_moves.failure_mode: Static stress can silently become a clinical endpoint.

author_reported: Quasi-static compression cannot evaluate fatigue; porosity may affect fatigue (S016:C01).
One individual's anatomy and one L3-L4 context limit generalizability (S016:C02).
Biological performance/osteointegration and only one TPMS design were not tested; animal and long-term work is needed (S016:C02).
reader_identified: No mesh convergence, constitutive verification, or parameter uncertainty analysis is reported.
Healthy ROM comparison is a baseline check, not implant-stress validation; direct stress measurements are absent.
Bonded bone-prosthesis and rigid screw connections omit slip, micromotion, imperfect contact, and endplate damage.
Triplicate polyurethane/quasi-static tests do not reproduce osteoporotic endplates, cycles, surgery, or fusion.
Global porosity within 2% does not quantify local SLM defects, anisotropy, roughness, or fatigue-critical flaws.
likely_bias_direction: Ideal bonded interfaces and single healthy anatomy likely favor designed stability.
Polyurethane and quasi-static loading may overestimate subsidence resistance relative to osteoporotic cyclic conditions.
One selected gyroid gradient may appear superior to untested gradients/TPMS.
Modulus-matching rationale may favor lower stress without fusion evidence.
limitations.scope_boundary: Evidence supports a mechanical comparison of one topology+gradient-gyroid Ti-6Al-4V AVI against TMC and truss+fluorite in a single-subject FE context and triplicate quasi-static tests; it does not demonstrate fatigue life, osteointegration, fusion, or clinical effectiveness.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: Explain hierarchical implant design by assigning macro-framework and microarchitecture distinct mechanical/biological roles before synthesis.
writing_capability_candidates.manuscript_use: Introduction, design rationale, and mechanistic Discussion.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: A two-scale rationale does not establish biology without interface ingrowth and long-term loading.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: Report nominal architecture, SLM/post-processing state, and as-built porosity as separate evidence states.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: A global porosity check does not quantify local defects, roughness, or fatigue flaws.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: Use baseline ROM benchmarking as a bounded check while keeping implant stress predictions and bench outcomes in separate validation lanes.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: Healthy ROM agreement does not validate postoperative implant stress magnitudes.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: Pair posture-resolved stress maps with matched mechanical metrics, then state the fatigue/biology/clinical endpoint ceiling.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: Static stress and polyurethane subsidence do not establish cyclic survival, fusion, or clinical safety.

critical_weaknesses: Single anatomy and idealized bonded interfaces.
No mesh/parameter uncertainty or implant-specific stress validation.
Triplicate quasi-static tests without fatigue, biological, or clinical outcomes.

summary_zh: 本文把宏观 SIMP 拓扑框架与轴向梯度 Gyroid TPMS 结合，比较其与 TMC、truss+fluorite AVI 的静态力学表现。梯度设计名义总孔隙率 55%（端部 70%、中央 40%），SLM 实测偏差小于 2%；单一健康男性 L1-L5 模型在六种姿态下显示植入体和骨-植入界面应力下降。三重复实验中 3 mm 下沉载荷为 2714±22 N，压缩刚度 63.97±0.35 kN/mm、屈服载荷 54.33±0.97 kN。ROM 对照只验证了基线模型，未验证植入体应力；聚氨酯准静态试验也不能替代疲劳、骨整合、融合或临床结果。
reader_notes: 已按 packet 顺序阅读全部 30 个非 reference chunk（S001:C01 至 S028:C01），包括 acknowledgements、trial-number、data/ethics 等短段，未遗漏。
全文 article kind 为原始混合计算-实验研究；screening 的 in_vivo_animal、clinical_or_observational 和 biological cues 未形成实际动物/临床端点。
明确记录 nominal 55% 与 as-built 偏差 <2%，以及 single-subject、bonded interface、quasi-static、无疲劳/骨整合等边界。
FE stress 是 predicted，subsidence/compression 是 measured bench outcomes；ROM 外部比较仅作为健康基线验证。
